name: Ink Wizarder (Legendary Inquisitor Archetype)
body:
Many wizard organizations are structured like religions, with rules, customs, and protocols dictating the actions and decisions of these magical factions. Such wizardly orders often police their own by training and employing “ink wizarders”, so named because they are wizards more on ink and paper certification than in the actual classical education of magic. No less stern and ruthless than their religious counterparts, ink wizarders seek out and judge those who misuse magic for ill reasons.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

An ink wizarder is proficient with all simple weapons, heavy crossbows, and light crossbows. Ink wizarders are also proficient with light armor and shields (except tower shields). An ink wizarder can cast spells while wearing light armor and using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance.

Like any other arcane spellcaster, an ink wizarder wearing medium or heavy armor incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multiclass ink wizarder still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.

This alters weapon and armor proficiencies.

Schooled

At 1st level, an ink wizarder chooses a school of magic. She gains the powers of this chosen school, treating her inquisitor level as her wizard level. She is not considered specialized in this arcane school and does not gain bonus spells from it.

This replaces domain.

Spellcasting

An ink wizarder’s spells are considered arcane spells rather than divine.

This alters spells.

Certified

At 3rd level, an ink wizarder can treat her inquisitor levels as wizard levels for the purpose of qualifying for feats.

This replaces solo tactics.

Wizardly Magic

At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, the ink wizarder adds one wizard spell of her choice to her spell list and list of spells known. This spell must be of a level she can cast.

This replaces teamwork feats.
